title: Fed Expected to Keep Raising Rates Until Inflation Cools
summary: Kelsey Berro, Fixed Income Portfolio Manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, discussed the Federal Reserve's challenging position amid recent disinflationary signals. Despite expectations for a modest 0.2% month-over-month increase in core CPI and relatively moderate inflation rates over several time horizons, the Fed remains cautious due to core PCE inflation running above 3%. Berro emphasized that a single data point will not dictate the Fed's next move, especially with key economic reports such as CPI, PPI, and payrolls scheduled in the coming weeks, alongside the upcoming Jackson Hole symposium. The market continues to price in potential rate hikes, reflecting the Fed's possible strategy of implementing 'insurance hikes' if inflation data remains elevated and the labor market stable. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Unpriced Food Inflation Threatens Volatile Bond Market
summary: Marie-Anne Allier, Fixed Income Fund Manager at Carmignac Gestion, discussed the current challenges facing bond markets amid rising energy prices and geopolitical tensions involving Iran. She noted that much of the negative impact from higher oil, gas, and energy prices is already priced into the market, with expectations of fewer interest rate cuts and potential hikes in the US and Europe. However, Allier highlighted a looming risk that is not yet fully reflected in bond prices: food inflation. She pointed to adverse weather conditions affecting harvests, disruptions to Ukraine's grain exports due to the conflict with Russia, and the potential volatility from El Niño as factors likely to trigger a new supply shock in food prices within the next six to twelve months. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Strategist Weighs September Fed Hike Amid Mixed Data
summary: Laureline Renauc-Chatelain, fixed income strategy lead at Pictet Wealth Management, discussed the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September. She noted that the recent payroll data was somewhat surprising but indicated a stable labor market that is not adding inflationary pressure. Despite noisy and downwardly revised employment figures, the key focus remains on upcoming Consumer Price Index (CPI) prints, which will heavily influence the Fed's decision. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Don't See Evidence That US is on 'Back Heels' Against Iran, Says Megan Ortagus
summary:
Morgan Ortagus, a former deputy presidential special envoy, said she doesn't see proof of the narrative that the US is on its 'back heels' in negotiations with Iran and that strategic patience is on the side of the United States. 
Ortagus said that while military options are still on the table, what the Iranian regime is most scared of is not the US or Israel, but the uprising of its own people. (Source: Bloomberg)
